findings.severity: substantive missing argument and incorrect source status
findings.finding: The author draft conflated the closed zero-index torus with the auxiliary punctured ambient and treated constructed relative rigidity as a remaining premise.
findings.resolution: The closed-torus proof now gives the minimal first-phase configuration, whole-frontier covering installation, finite annulus/disk failure alternative, component boundary-group commensurability, marked whole products and explicit contraction of a failure arc into one product end. Covering homotopy lifting contradicts its distinct endpoints. The puncture application is separate. The final consumer substitutes all three constructed rigidity families.

findings.severity: essential missing argument and incorrect termination measure
findings.finding: An unexplained finite repair list and a circles-first lexicographic measure did not describe the actual ordinary-projection construction.
findings.resolution: The one-dimensional finite double relation is distinguished from its finite exceptional pairs. Disjoint interior and half-space repair windows preserve complete branch images and give ordinary crossings globally. A separate minimum of boundary double-component count is reduced by spanning/nonspanning surgery; the two candidate rim words cannot both contract. Only at boundary count zero does induction remove interior circles. Whole-rim retention is up to individual circle homeomorphisms; collars later restore exact parametrizations.

findings.severity: incorrect generalization and missing side control
findings.finding: Boundary injectivity alone does not make an arbitrary local homeomorphism injective on a ball; Brown's pair conclusion also does not prescribe an arbitrary initial sphere parametrization.
findings.resolution: The additive lattice quotient is essential: disjoint translated frontiers force disjoint closures or nesting, and a linear functional maximized on the compact closure excludes nonzero nesting. Strict interval-coordinate bounds place the descended ball in the handle interior. Compactification retains separate inverse-image equations for sphere and closed ball, with a setwise boundary correspondence.

findings.finding: A bare simplicial approximation does not imply exact frontier preimage or PL regularity across the pasted boundary.
findings.resolution: A compact interior carrier retains a frontier neighborhood where the inverse realization is already target-PL. Hudson approximation fixes a closed subpolyhedron containing that neighborhood and keeps the moving homotopy in the interior. Pasting to the exterior identity through the fixed open overlap proves PL regularity and the exact boundary-preimage equation at every time.

findings.severity: essential missing construction and inverse-domain check
findings.finding: Rigidity was conflated with later protected placement; support alone did not establish PL regularity of the corrected original chart.
findings.resolution: Index one constructs matched slab maps and cancels two integer windings before inversion. Index two constructs a source meridian, exact collar rim and cut-prism regluing. In the application comparison A precedes placement Q. B=A^{-1}Q, Q(C) contained in A(P), and g^{-1}q(x)=pi(A^{-1}Qx) in pi(P) contained in N give the actual inverse domain. Both PL identity directions on N are retained. Full disk overlap equations prove injective index-two pasting. Radius-two and entire cylinder-frontier support hold throughout the final isotopy.

findings.severity: essential missing application of an available predecessor
findings.finding: An unmarked sphere does not select the required side; requesting a new compact-core contract field overlooks its existing universal protected-set quantifier.
findings.resolution: Protect A together with the complement of a puncture chart before applying Wall. The entire missing closed side then lies in that chart, excludes A and contains the puncture. Its exact frontier and compactness identify the bounded chart side to which Brown applies. This is derived locally from the completed protected-Wall theorem without strengthening the contract or requesting additional predecessor work.

findings.finding: Brown and Hudson locators needed primary-source verification, and Hamilton's compressed invocation obscured the special solid-torus argument.
findings.resolution: Read the primary Brown papers, Hudson Lemma 4.2 and control remark, Hamilton pp.64-68, and Waldhausen Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 6.1. Exact locators and proposed bibliography records appear below. The text explicitly avoids applying Waldhausen Theorem 6.1 to the compressible-boundary solid torus.
